newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong flies ancient giant turtles to Borneo.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong flies ancient giant turtles to Borneo.

text.p: Hong Kong returned 13 ancient "lucky" giant turtles -- the oldest thought to be aged over 200 years -- to their Borneo home in an airlift on Tuesday.
They included eight rescued by authorities from a tiny balcony in an urban high-rise apartment.
Unlike many endangered species recovered from time to time in Hong Kong, the amphibians were not destined for the cooking pot.
Known locally as temple terrapins, they are kept for luck -- turtles are a symbol of longevity in Chinese mythology.

Local carrier, Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd, flew the fortunate examples of Orlitia Borneensis, average age 100 years, to Kota Kinabalu, capital of the east Malaysian state of Sabah, at no charge, an airline spokeswoman said.
Five had been raised in local zoos but vets decided Hong Kong's climate was not suitable for the turtles which can grow to 80 cm (30 inches) across and weigh more than 50 kg (110 lb).
The eight rescued from a balcony were up for sale when inspectors from the Agriculture and Fisheries Department swooped.
